style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The second psalm to open with 'the LORD reigns', and the one that shows the King arriving: clouds and thick darkness around Him, fire running ahead, lightning lighting the world, the earth writhing, the mountains melting like wax. It is Sinai's weather, brought to a coronation. But the throne's foundation is not the storm -- it is righteousness and justice -- and the heavens announce that righteousness so that every people sees His glory. The idols' servants are shamed and the 'gods' themselves are ordered to bow, a line the Greek Psalter rendered 'all His angels' and Hebrews 1:6 echoes of the angels worshiping the Son; Zion hears and is glad; the LORD is Most High over all the earth. Then the psalm turns to the congregation with its one ethical command -- you who love the LORD, hate evil -- and its promise: He guards His faithful, rescues them from the wicked, and has light sown for the righteous, seed in the ground with a harvest coming. It ends on Psalm 30:4's line -- give thanks to the memorial of His holiness -- prefaced by Psalm 32:11's summons: be glad in the LORD, you righteous. The islands were told to be glad in the first verse; the righteous are told in the last.

1.text: The LORD reigns! Let the earth exult; let the many coastlands be glad.
1.amp: The LORD [YHWH] reigns [malak]; let the earth [eretz] rejoice [gil -- exult]; let the multitude ['many, or, great isles', rav, the KJV margin] of isles [iy -- coastlands, islands] be glad [samach] thereof.
1.notes: YHWH malakh tagel ha-aretz (H4427, H1523, H776): the reign announced, and the earth told to spin with joy -- yismechu iyyim rabbim (H8055, H339, H7227): the many iyyim, the coastlands and islands, the far edges of the map where the Gentiles lived (cf. Isaiah 42:4). The King's inauguration is good news to the distant.

2.text: Cloud and thick darkness are all around Him; righteousness and justice are what His throne is founded on.
2.amp: Clouds [anan] and darkness [araphel -- thick darkness] are round about [sabib] Him: righteousness [tsedek] and judgment [mishpat -- justice] are the habitation ['establishment', makon -- foundation, the KJV margin] of His throne [kisse].
2.notes: anan va-araphel sevivav (H6051, H6205, H5439): Sinai's cloud and thick darkness around Him -- the King is unseen. tsedek u-mishpat mekhon kisso (H6664, H4941, H4349, H3678): but the throne's FOUNDATION is visible: righteousness and justice, Psalm 89:14's pair. What you cannot see is His face; what you can see is His fairness.

3.text: A fire goes ahead of Him and burns up His adversaries on every side.
3.amp: A fire [esh] goes [yalak] before [panim] Him, and burns up [lahat -- blazes, consumes] His enemies [tsar -- adversaries] round about [sabib].
3.notes: esh le-phanav telekh (H784, H6440, H3212): fire as the King's outrider -- u-telahet sabib tsarav (H3857, H5439, H6862): blazing around His adversaries. Psalm 50:3's fire, and Hebrews 12:29's consuming God.

4.text: His lightnings light up the world; the earth sees, and writhes.
4.amp: His lightnings [baraq] enlightened [or -- lit up] the world [tebel]: the earth [eretz] saw [raah], and trembled [chul -- writhed].
4.notes: heiru beraqav tebel (H215, H1300, H8398): the lightning that lights the inhabited world -- raatah va-tachel ha-aretz (H7200, H2342, H776): the earth sees and chul, writhes like a woman in labor -- Psalm 29:8's verb. Psalm 77:18 opens with the same clause -- the lightnings lighting the world -- with the Red Sea storm remembered.

5.text: The mountains melt like wax before the face of the LORD, before the face of the Lord of all the earth.
5.amp: The hills [har] melted [masas] like wax [donag] at the presence [panim] of the LORD [YHWH], at the presence of the Lord [Adon] of the whole earth [eretz].
5.notes: harim ka-donag namassu (H2022, H1749, H4549): mountains melting like wax -- Micah 1:4's picture -- mi-liphne YHWH, mi-liphne Adon kol-ha-aretz (H6440, H3068, H113, H776): the Master of the whole earth, the title of Joshua 3:11 at the Jordan. The most permanent things liquefy when He arrives.

6.text: The heavens announce His righteousness, and every people has seen His glory.
6.amp: The heavens [shamayim] declare [nagad] His righteousness [tsedek], and all the people [am] see [raah] His glory [kabod].
6.notes: higgidu ha-shamayim tsidqo (H5046, H8064, H6664): Psalm 19:1's heavens, declaring not now His glory but His RIGHTEOUSNESS -- the exact line of Psalm 50:6 -- ve-rau kol-ha-ammim kebodo (H7200, H5971, H3519): and all the peoples see His glory. The storm of verses 2-5 was a public event.

7.text: Let all who serve carved images be put to shame -- those who boast in worthless idols. Bow down to Him, all you gods!
7.amp: Confounded [bosh] be all they that serve [abad] graven images [pesel], that boast [halal] themselves of idols [elil -- worthless things]: worship [shachah -- bow down] Him, all ye gods [elohim].
7.notes: yevoshu kol-obede phesel (H954, H5647, H6459): the idol-servers ashamed -- ha-mithalelim ba-elilim (H1984, H457): who BOAST -- the same halal as praise, pointed at nothings: elil, 'worthless thing', which many hear as a contemptuous play on El, 'God' -- a godling, a no-god. hishtachavu-lo kol-elohim (H7812, H430): bow to Him, all you gods -- whatever the 'gods' are, they kneel; the Greek Psalter read 'all His angels' here, and Hebrews 1:6 echoes that line (its wording also matches the Greek of Deuteronomy 32:43) of the angels worshiping the Son.

8.text: Zion heard it and was glad, and the daughters of Judah exulted, because of Your judgments, O LORD.
8.amp: Zion [Tsiyyon] heard [shama], and was glad [samach]; and the daughters [bath] of Judah [Yehudah] rejoiced [gil -- exulted] because of Your judgments [mishpat], O LORD [YHWH].
8.notes: shameah va-tismach Tsiyyon (H8085, H8055, H6726): Zion HEARD -- the news of the reign reaching the city -- va-tagelnah benot Yehudah (H1523, H1323, H3063): the daughters of Judah, the towns around the capital, exulting le-maan mishpatekha (H4941): because of Your judgments. The judgments the wicked fear are the ones the faithful celebrate.

9.text: For You, O LORD, are Most High over all the earth; You are raised far above all gods.
9.amp: For You, LORD [YHWH], are high above [Elyon -- Most High] all the earth [eretz]: You are exalted [alah] far above [meod] all gods [elohim].
9.notes: ki-attah YHWH Elyon al-kol-ha-aretz (H5945, H776): Elyon, the Most High, as a predicate -- meod naaleta al-kol-elohim (H3966, H5927, H430): very much gone up above all gods -- the alah of Psalm 47:5 and 9. Verse 7's kneeling gods are now measured: far below.

10.text: You who love the LORD -- hate evil! He guards the souls of His faithful ones; He rescues them from the hand of the wicked.
10.amp: Ye that love [ahab] the LORD [YHWH], hate [sane] evil [ra]: He preserves [shamar -- guards] the souls [nephesh] of His saints [chasid -- covenant-faithful ones]; He delivers [natsal] them out of the hand [yad] of the wicked [rasha].
10.notes: ohave YHWH sinu ra (H157, H8130, H7451): the ethical hinge of the psalm -- love for the LORD entails hatred of evil; the two are one loyalty facing two ways (cf. Romans 12:9; Amos 5:15). shomer naphshot chasidav (H8104, H5315, H2623), mi-yad reshaim yatsilem (H3027, H7563, H5337): the guarding and the rescuing are the King's side of the covenant.

11.text: Light lies sown for the righteous man, and gladness for those whose heart is straight.
11.amp: Light [or] is sown [zara] for the righteous [tsaddiq], and gladness [simchah] for the upright [yashar] in heart [leb].
11.notes: or zarua la-tsaddiq (H216, H2232, H6662): light SOWN -- planted like seed, not yet harvested; the righteous live between the sowing and the reaping of their light -- u-le-yishre-leb simchah (H3477, H3820, H8057): and gladness for the straight of heart. A promise with a growing season built in (cf. Psalm 126:5-6).

12.text: Be glad in the LORD, you righteous ones, and give thanks to His holy Name -- the memorial of His holiness!
12.amp: Rejoice [samach] in the LORD [YHWH], ye righteous [tsaddiq]; and give thanks [yadah] at the remembrance ['to the memorial', zeker, the KJV margin] of His holiness [qodesh].
12.notes: simchu tsaddiqim ba-YHWH (H8055, H6662): the gladness sown in verse 11 comes up as a command -- ve-hodu le-zekher qodsho (H3034, H2143, H6944): give thanks to His holy memorial, the Name by which He is remembered, Psalm 30:4's line word for word. The reign that began by terrifying the earth ends by gladdening the righteous.
